Our first big customer left us 5 months in. Best thing that ever happened to Ledgerline.

#Startups #SaaS #Leadership #CustomerSuccess #Growth

1,200 repositories.

When we launched Patchwork CI, we promised it would always be free for open source. People told us we were crazy. How would we make money?

Today we run on 1,200 repositories. About 900 are open source.

Here's the part that surprised me. Across all those repos, 1 in 7 CI failures was a flaky test. One in seven. Think about how many hours you've lost staring at a red build that was never broken.

Open source gave us more than users. It gave us data, feedback, and a community. Our most-requested feature, GitLab support, came straight from OSS maintainers. We shipped it on November 12.

Giving back is not charity. It is strategy.

#OpenSource #DevOps #CI #DeveloperExperience #BuildInPublic

I want to tell you why Fernway Studio stopped billing by the hour.

#Entrepreneurship #Africa #Shopify #AgencyLife #Pricing

We built a good-looking app. Nobody used it.

When we launched Rotaship, we were proud of how sleek it looked. We figured restaurant staff would like it.

They didn't. Only 12% of staff even opened it in the first month.

That stung. But it taught us something: we weren't solving the real problem. We were adding to it.

Restaurant teams don't want another app. They live on WhatsApp.

So in 2025 we made the call. We moved everything into WhatsApp.

It worked. 140 outlets now use it, and the median reply time to shift messages is under 20 minutes.

If you're building for busy people, build where they already are. Don't ask them to come to you.

Sometimes the best product decision is letting go of the thing you love.

You've sold before and you liked it. You like chasing a yes, you like the phone, you don't need a manager standing over you. You'd rather join a small team where your name is on the results than a big one where it isn't.

1,000 families.

#Startups #Portugal #Parenting #FemaleFounders #Gratitude

I spent 11 years in a clinic. Then I quit.

I loved being a vet. I still do. But something kept eating at me.

Pets would come in so terrified we had to sedate them just to look in their ears. Every single time, I thought: there has to be a better way.

So in 2023 I founded Doorstep Vet.

The idea is simple. Same quality care, but at home, where your pet actually feels safe.

Our 4 vets now do about 30 home visits a week. Every visit reminds me why I left.

Calmer pets. Happier owners. Better medicine.

Sometimes walking away is the brave thing.

#Veterinary #PetCare #Melbourne #Entrepreneurship #FollowYourPassion

We put our prices up 50%. Here is how it went.

September was nerve-racking. We took Tabwise from $8 to $12 per user per month, and I wasn't sure how people would take it.

The reason was simple: support costs per customer had doubled since we launched. Either we cut corners on quality or we charged what the product was actually worth.

We went with charging what it's worth.

Existing customers didn't get punished for it, though. Anyone already on the plan kept paying $8 for another 12 months.

So what happened next? In the two months after the increase, just 2 of our 140 customers left.

Two out of 140.

What I took from this: people don't buy software, they buy results. Price for the results.

Founders, when did you last raise your prices?

#SaaS #Pricing #StartupLessons #Growth #B2B

400 labels shipped with a faulty battery contact.

As a young hardware startup, it would have been easy to cut corners. But that is not who we are.

We did not stop there. We introduced a 100% contact test at the factory. Since then, we have had zero contact failures across 6,000 labels.

Mistakes do not define you. How you respond to them does.

To all the hardware founders out there: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they never happen again.
